from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["Imagine a globe's surface.", "Any two opposite points exist.", "Temperatures at these points match.", "Antipodal points share conditions.", "This is Borsuk-Ulam's insight."]
        self.setup_layout("Intuitive Hook: Antipodal Points", lecture_lines)
        
        # Elements
        sphere = Sphere(radius=1.5, color=BLUE, fill_opacity=0.3)
        sphere.set_stroke(WHITE, opacity=0.5)
        self.place_in_area(sphere, 'A3', 'F5')
        
        # Define antipodal points
        p1 = Dot(color="#FF5733", radius=0.1)
        p2 = Dot(color="#33FF57", radius=0.1)
        
        # Position points on the sphere using spherical coordinates conversion
        def get_point(phi, theta, r=1.5):
            return np.array([r * np.sin(phi) * np.cos(theta), r * np.sin(phi) * np.sin(theta), r * np.cos(phi)])
        
        p1.move_to(sphere.get_center() + get_point(PI/4, PI/4))
        p2.move_to(sphere.get_center() + get_point(PI - PI/4, PI + PI/4))
        
        # Pulse animation setup
        def pulse(mob, dt):
            mob.radius = 0.1 + 0.05 * np.sin(self.time * 5)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(Create(sphere), run_time=1)
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFD700")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(p1), FadeIn(p2), run_time=1)
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFD700")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(Indicate(p1), Indicate(p2), run_time=1)
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFD700")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        p1.add_updater(pulse)
        p2.add_updater(pulse)
        self.play(Rotate(sphere, angle=PI/2, axis=UP), run_time=2)
        self.lecture[3].set_color("#FFD700")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        p1.remove_updater(pulse)
        p2.remove_updater(pulse)
        self.play(FadeOut(p1), FadeOut(p2), run_time=1)
        self.lecture[4].set_color("#FFD700")
        self.wait(1)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["Necklace beads represent intervals.", "Continuous paths model discrete objects.", "Topology solves combinatorics tasks."]
        self.setup_layout("Transition: From Spheres to Necklaces", lecture_lines)
        
        # --- Visual Elements ---
        
        # Initial Necklace: A group of colored circles
        beads = VGroup(*[Circle(radius=0.3, fill_opacity=0.8, color=color) 
                        for color in [YELLOW, GRAY, YELLOW, GRAY, YELLOW, GRAY]])
        beads.arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        self.place_at_grid(beads, 'B2', scale_factor=1.0)
        
        # Line representation (initially invisible)
        line = Line(start=np.array([-2, 0, 0]), end=np.array([2, 0, 0]), color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(line, 'D3', scale_factor=1.0)
        line.set_opacity(0)
        
        # Markers
        markers = VGroup(*[Line(UP*0.2, DOWN*0.2, color=RED) for _ in range(4)])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(beads))
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(BLUE)
        # Transform beads to lie on the line
        self.play(
            FadeIn(line),
            beads.animate.arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.05).move_to(line.get_center())
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(GREEN)
        # Show markers on the line
        for i, m in enumerate(markers):
            m.move_to(line.point_from_proportion(0.2 * (i+1)))
        self.play(Create(markers))
        self.wait(1)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Stolen Necklace Problem", [
            "Two thieves share loot.", 
            "Cut necklaces perfectly now.", 
            "Fair division uses cuts.", 
            "Borsuk-Ulam guarantees equitable splits.", 
            "Optimal cuts divide necklaces."
        ])
        
        # Setup visual elements
        necklace = Line(LEFT*2.5, RIGHT*2.5, stroke_width=8, color=YELLOW)
        beads = VGroup(*[Circle(radius=0.15, fill_opacity=1, color=color) 
                         for color in [RED, BLUE]*5]).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.2)
        necklace_full = VGroup(necklace, beads).shift(UP*1)
        self.place_at_grid(necklace_full, 'B2')
        
        thief1 = Text("Thief 1", color=BLUE).shift(DOWN*1.5 + LEFT*1)
        thief2 = Text("Thief 2", color=RED).shift(DOWN*1.5 + RIGHT*1)
        self.add(thief1, thief2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(necklace_full), Write(thief1), Write(thief2))
        self.lecture[0].set_color(BLUE)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        cuts = VGroup(*[DashedLine(UP*0.5, DOWN*0.5, color="#FF4500") for _ in range(2)])

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===

outline.topic: The Borsuk-Ulam Theorem and the Stolen Necklace Problem

sections.title: Intuitive Hook: The antipodal points
sections.content: Introduce the concept of a sphere and antipodal points (two points exactly opposite on a sphere). State the core premise: If we look at temperature or pressure on Earth, there must exist two opposite points with identical conditions.
sections.example: Visualize a 3D Earth globe; as you rotate it, identify two points 'North Pole' and 'South Pole' mapping to a shared weather condition value.

sections.title: The Borsuk-Ulam Theorem (Mathematical Foundation)
sections.content: Formalize the theorem: Any continuous function from an n-sphere to n-dimensional Euclidean space maps at least one pair of antipodal points to the same value. Use a visual 'height mapping' animation on a topographical map.
sections.example: A hiker walking around a mountain range; the theorem guarantees there are always two opposite spots on the mountain with the exact same altitude.

sections.title: Transition: From Spheres to Necklaces
sections.content: Bridge the gap: Explain how we represent discrete items (like beads on a necklace) as a continuous interval (0 to 1). This connects topology to combinatorial problems.
sections.example: An animation showing beads of two colors (gold and silver) being 'stretched' along a line segment to represent their density distribution.

sections.title: The Stolen Necklace Problem
sections.content: Define the problem: Two thieves steal a necklace with n types of beads. They want to cut it into pieces such that each thief gets exactly half of each type of bead. State the theorem: For k thieves and n types of beads, at most k(n-1) cuts are needed.
sections.example: Two burglars (Alice and Bob) with a necklace containing 10 rubies and 10 diamonds. The animation shows them making precise cuts to split the loot perfectly using the Borsuk-Ulam result.

sections.title: Summary and Real-world Insight
sections.content: Conclude by emphasizing the beauty of 'Topological Combinatorics': how high-level geometry provides efficient algorithmic solutions for fair division problems.
sections.example: Final slide showing a complex cake-cutting machine or a resource allocation dashboard using these principles to ensure fairness in distribution.
